The invention relates to an application assembly for coating confectionery products. The assembly comprises a housing that defines a product-coating void configured to receive a confectionery product. At least one receptacle is provided for holding a coating material, with the receptacle including supply holes through which the coating material can flow into the product-coating void.

Each receptacle is equipped with one or more applicator members arranged to transfer the coating material onto the surface of the confectionery product. The applicator members include cavities designed to collect and temporarily store excess coating material when the product remains stationary within the assembly. This arrangement helps control the application of the coating material and reduces unwanted accumulation on the product.

The invention also encompasses a method for partially coating confectionery products using the application assembly.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to an assembly and method for applying a coating material to selected portions of confectionery products. The assembly includes a housing that defines a coating void through which, or within which, a confectionery product is positioned during a coating operation. One or more receptacles associated with the housing hold a flowable coating material, such as chocolate, icing, glaze, syrup, or another edible composition. Supply holes provide fluid communication between the receptacles and applicator members arranged adjacent to the coating void.

During operation, coating material flows from the receptacles through the supply holes to the applicator members. As a confectionery product moves through or is positioned in the coating void, the applicator members contact, or are placed sufficiently close to, selected surfaces of the product and transfer the coating material onto those surfaces. The location, shape, and orientation of the applicator members may be selected so that only predetermined portions of the product are coated, while other portions remain substantially uncoated. This permits repeatable partial coating without immersing the entire product in a coating bath.

Each applicator member may include an applicator cavity configured to receive excess coating material. When a product remains stationary relative to the housing, coating material that would otherwise continue accumulating on the product can collect within the applicator cavity. The cavity therefore acts as a temporary reservoir, reducing uncontrolled transfer, dripping, and localized buildup. When relative movement resumes, coating stored in the cavity may again be made available for application to the product.

In an exemplary method, the receptacles are filled with coating material, and the material is delivered through the supply holes to the applicator members. A confectionery product is then introduced into the coating void and moved relative to the applicator members so that coating is deposited on selected regions of the product. If movement is interrupted, excess material is received and retained in the applicator cavities. The product may subsequently be removed, advanced for further processing, or subjected to cooling or setting to solidify the applied coating.

The disclosed arrangement provides controlled and efficient partial coating of confectionery products. By collecting excess material near the point of application, the assembly can improve coating consistency, reduce waste and unwanted accumulation, and accommodate intermittent product movement in automated or semi-automated production systems.

### The Power of “The”

“The” may be one of the smallest words in English, but it plays an essential role in communication. Known as the definite article, it points to a specific person, place, object, or idea. Saying “a book” could mean any book, while “the book” refers to one that is already known or clearly identified.

Beyond grammar, “the” creates focus and significance. Expressions such as “the future,” “the truth,” and “the world” suggest ideas that feel unique or universally understood. Although it often goes unnoticed, “the” gives language clarity, precision, and shared meaning.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in formal patent language, an apparatus and method for applying a partial coating to confectionery products, including a cavity for storing accumulated coating material when a product remains static.
counterfactuals.output:
### Apparatus

An apparatus for applying a coating material to a selected portion of a confectionery product, the apparatus comprising:

a support configured to receive and retain the confectionery product at a coating position;

a coating applicator arranged to discharge a flow of coating material toward the coating position such that the flow contacts less than an entirety of an exterior surface of the confectionery product;

a drive mechanism configured to produce relative movement between the confectionery product and the coating applicator during a coating operation; and

a coating-accumulation cavity disposed adjacent to and below at least a portion of the coating position, the coating-accumulation cavity being configured to receive and temporarily store coating material discharged while the confectionery product remains substantially static relative to the coating applicator, thereby limiting accumulation of the coating material on the confectionery product.

In certain embodiments, the support comprises a conveyor having one or more product-engaging members configured to expose a lower, lateral, or end portion of the confectionery product to the discharged coating material. The coating applicator may comprise a nozzle, manifold, curtain-forming outlet, dipping member, spray head, or combination thereof. The coating-accumulation cavity may be formed as a recess in the support, in a product carrier, or in a collection member positioned beneath the product carrier.

The cavity may have an inlet opening aligned with the discharged flow and a volume sufficient to receive coating material delivered during a predetermined dwell or interruption period. A drain, recirculation conduit, heating element, or temperature-control passage may be coupled to the cavity to facilitate removal, reuse, or maintenance of the coating material in a flowable condition.

A controller may be operatively connected to the drive mechanism and the coating applicator. Upon detecting stoppage or reduced movement of the confectionery product, the controller may interrupt or reduce discharge of the coating material. The coating-accumulation cavity receives coating material discharged before cessation or reduction of the flow and, optionally, coating material continuing to be discharged during the stoppage.

### Method

A method of partially coating a confectionery product comprises:

positioning the confectionery product on a support at a coating position;

discharging a coating material from a coating applicator toward the confectionery product;

producing relative movement between the confectionery product and the coating applicator such that the coating material is applied to a selected portion, but not an entirety, of an exterior surface of the confectionery product;

detecting or permitting a condition in which the confectionery product remains substantially static relative to the coating applicator while coating material is present at the coating position; and

receiving coating material accumulating during the static condition within a coating-accumulation cavity adjacent to the confectionery product, thereby reducing uncontrolled buildup of coating material on the confectionery product.

The method may further comprise interrupting or reducing discharge of the coating material in response to the static condition, maintaining the accumulated coating material at a selected temperature, draining the accumulated coating material from the cavity, and returning at least a portion of the drained coating material to a coating-material supply.

The confectionery product may comprise a bar, biscuit, wafer, cake, candy, frozen confection, or molded confectionery article, and the coating material may comprise chocolate, compound coating, icing, glaze, fat-based coating, sugar-based coating, or another edible flowable composition.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
